testkit 0.1.0

A compact assertion and reporting library that brings a familiar pytest-shaped workflow to Basalt source tests without requiring a framework runtime.

Download archive View source

README

Assertions that read like tests

Each assertion returns 1 for success and 0 for failure. Pass the result to testkit::run to print a named PASSED or FAILED line, add the returned failure count, and finish with testkit::summary.

Import

include "packages/testkit/0.1.0/src/testkit.basalt"

API

FunctionBehavior
assert_true(actual)Passes when a boolean expression is true.
assert_int(actual, expected)Exact equality for integer values.
assert_bool(actual, expected)Exact equality for boolean values.
assert_char(actual, expected)Exact equality for character values.
assert_string(actual, expected)Byte-oriented NUL-terminated string equality.
assert_between(value, minimum, maximum)Inclusive integer range check.
assert_not_int(actual, unexpected)Passes when integer values differ.
assert_f64_close(actual, expected, tolerance)Absolute-difference floating-point check.
run(name, passed)Prints a named result and returns a failure increment.
summary(total, failures)Prints totals and returns the failure count.

Pytest-like fixture

include "packages/testkit/0.1.0/src/testkit.basalt"

func main(): int {
  let total: int = 0;
  let failures: int = 0;
  total += 1;
  failures += testkit::run(
    "test_addition",
    testkit::assert_int(2 + 2, 4)
  );
  return testkit::summary(total, failures);
}

Compatibility

The original check_* functions remain available as aliases, so existing package fixtures can migrate incrementally to the clearer assert_* names.
